blocks.p: A ZNIX window shows an action only when it can be done: now, or after a step that ZNIX takes for you, such as walking over to the thing or taking off a hat. An action that needs something the character lacks, such as a tool, an ingredient, parts or a skill level, is hidden. An action that makes no sense at the moment, such as *Put out* on a fire that is already out, is gone, and is never hinted at.

Figure 6-1 shows the *Hair and beard* section of the *Character* window for a character with no scissors or razor. The actions the character cannot do yet are not listed one by one; they fold into a single row at the foot of the section, which says how many there are.

caption: Figure 6-1
Folded, the default: what cannot be done yet folds into one row.

blocks.p: To open the folded row, click it. The hidden actions then show, grayed, each with a line that says what it needs. Whether the row is open or closed is remembered for the rest of the session.

marks.text: What you can't do yet folds into one row: "5 more with the right things".

sticky.text: What you can't do yet folds into one row.

blocks.p: What is shown of the hidden actions is set by *Hidden actions*, in *Options*, *ZeD setup*. It is a pop-up menu with three choices:

list: *Folded*, the default: the hidden actions fold into one row.
*Show all*: each hidden action, grayed, with what it needs.
*Hide*: the hidden actions are not hinted at.

blocks.p: Figure 6-2 shows *Show all* on the same section of the *Character* window. Each style the character cannot do yet is listed in gray, and the line beside it names what it needs. A hint names only what the game itself would show; it never names a recipe the character has not learned.

caption: Figure 6-2
Show all: the same actions, grayed, each with what it needs.

blocks.note: The setting is in *ZeD setup* only.

marks.text: Show all lists the same actions, grayed, each with what it needs.

sticky.text: Show all: grayed, with what each needs.
